why: The vocabulary the privacy tests scan room state for.
It lives in JSON rather than TypeScript on purpose: check 5 of
scripts/check-invariants.sh greps every .ts file under packages/lobby/src
for exactly these words and fails the build when it finds one, so a test
that spelled them in TypeScript would trip the very gate it exists to
reinforce. Keeping the list as data satisfies both: the scanner sees no
financial vocabulary in lobby code, and the test still has real strings to
Nothing here may be a word spellable in hexadecimal alone — an ephemeral
gameId is 16 hex characters, so a word like 'fee' would match by chance
roughly once in every three hundred sessions and make the test flaky.
For the same reason the wei-scale pattern requires 17 digits rather than
15: an identifier that happens to be all digits is only 16 long.
